_meta.description: Default sampling/generation parameter values and applicability per provider+wrapper combination. Used to backfill 'framework_default' / 'not_applicable' / 'unknown' provenance tiers for parameters NOT found explicitly at a call site. Never used to override an explicit value found in source.
_meta.verification_notes: Verified against current OpenAI/Azure OpenAI/Anthropic/LangChain/AWS Bedrock documentation as of last_verified. Values marked 'unknown' in wrapper/family tables below reflect cases where no numeric default is documented publicly (not an oversight) -- see per-entry 'note' fields. These values drift with provider API versions and should be re-verified periodically.

tier_meaning.framework_default: Parameter not found in code, but the wrapper/SDK has a known, documented default. 'value' carries that default.
tier_meaning.not_applicable: Parameter does not exist / is rejected / is fixed-and-non-configurable for this provider+wrapper (or model family). No 'value' is recorded -- the concept of a 'default' does not apply.
tier_meaning.unknown: Parameter not found in code, and no reliable default is known (either genuinely unbounded/unset, or provider does not publish a default). No 'value' is recorded -- absence should be read as 'set dynamically somewhere unseen', not 'using a default'.

top_k.note: OpenAI chat completions API has no top_k parameter

max_tokens.note: no fixed default -- generation is unbounded up to the model's context/output limit if unset

stop.note: no stop sequences configured by default

seed.note: no seed by default -- sampling is non-deterministic unless explicitly set

openai_reasoning._source: OpenAI reasoning models guide; Azure OpenAI reasoning models docs; community-confirmed 400 error behavior for o1/o3/o4/gpt-5 series

temperature.note: fixed/rejected on reasoning models -- API returns 400 if set to a non-default value

max_tokens.note: reasoning models use max_completion_tokens; no fixed numeric default, and reasoning tokens also consume this budget

azure_openai_raw_sdk._source: Azure/azure-rest-api-specs AzureOpenAI inference.yaml -- mirrors raw OpenAI chat completions defaults

max_tokens.note: no fixed default -- unbounded up to model limit if unset

azure_openai_reasoning._source: Microsoft Learn: Azure OpenAI reasoning models (o-series, gpt-5 series) -- 'Not Supported' parameter list

max_tokens.note: classic max_tokens is explicitly unsupported on Azure reasoning models; use max_completion_tokens, which has no fixed default

anthropic_raw_sdk._source: Anthropic Messages API reference (anthropic-sdk-python message_create_params.py); platform.claude.com Messages API docs

top_k.note: applicable but unset by default on most models; not supported at all on Claude Opus 4.7+ (not modeled here)

max_tokens.note: REQUIRED parameter with no default per Anthropic docs -- absence means it is set dynamically elsewhere, not defaulted

frequency_penalty.note: not an Anthropic Messages API parameter

presence_penalty.note: not an Anthropic Messages API parameter

seed.note: not an Anthropic Messages API parameter

n.note: not an Anthropic Messages API parameter

langchain_chatopenai._source: langchain-ai/langchain ChatOpenAI Pydantic field defaults (classic langchain.chat_models.openai / langchain.llms.openai); NOTE: newer langchain_openai releases may leave temperature unset (None), which falls through to the raw OpenAI SDK default of 1.0 instead -- version-dependent, re-verify if targeting langchain_openai>=0.2

temperature.note: distinct from raw OpenAI SDK default of 1.0 -- this is the wrapper's own Pydantic field default

top_p.note: no wrapper-level field default documented; falls through to model_kwargs pass-through

max_tokens.note: wrapper field default is None -- unbounded, same as raw SDK

n.note: wrapper Pydantic field default: n: int = 1

langchain_chatanthropic._source: no confirmed wrapper-level field defaults found -- all params intentionally left unknown rather than guessed

bedrock_model_families._note: Keyed by model-ID prefix pattern (matched against declared_model). Bedrock has no single wrapper-wide default -- each underlying model family defines its own request-body defaults, so this is intentionally nested rather than a flat 'bedrock' entry.
